q2_gaps: title-cased office phrase whose premodifier is itself a proper noun ("the Cauldron Hall Warden") — the mechanical name cue ("the name is exactly its capitalized run of words") would make the whole run one name, while the proper-noun-premodifying-a-common-noun-head rule (whose examples all have a lowercase head: "a Northgate spokesman") splits it into named entity + common-noun head; the instruction set does not say which wins when the head noun is capitalized too
definite predicate nominal / office equative ("X is THE N") — there is no carrier for the uniqueness the definite article states, so it is encoded exactly like the indefinite "X is a N"
notes: Under the reading that "Cauldron Hall" is the name and "Warden" the head noun, the parse follows the Northgate-spokesman pattern exactly — head-noun typing predicated of Hesper, the opaque (Possession hesper cauldron_hall) in possessed-first order, and the kind word inside the name licensing (Member cauldron_hall hall).
